name: wraptool
description: Wire a dev container's AI coding harness to a host-side wraptool MCP server. Wiring-only major (see design/harness/unified-harness-pool.md §12): this feature no longer installs the harness binary. The binary comes from the host's shared harness pool `runtime/` tree (built by `wraptool harness install <name>`) — `wraptool up` mounts it read-only at /opt/wraptool-harness/runtime and appends its bin/ to PATH automatically. A container started WITHOUT `wraptool up` (plain `devcontainer up`, editor-managed) still gets HOME pinning + PATH wiring from this feature, but no binary unless you declare the mount yourself, e.g.: { "mounts": [ "source=${localEnv:HOME}/.local/share/wraptool/harness-pool/runtime,target=/opt/wraptool-harness/runtime,type=bind,readonly" ] } — rewrite the source for your OS per §12.3 (macOS: '${localEnv:HOME}/Library/Application Support/wraptool/harness-pool/runtime'; Windows: HOME must be set). The `harness` option now only selects which MCP config shape `connect` writes. The old provisioning major (`:0`) remains published for existing configs that still set `provision`/`version`, but is deprecated — new setups should adopt this major plus `wraptool harness install`.

harness.description: Which harness this feature wires — the MCP config shape connect writes. No longer selects an installer: the binary is not provisioned by this feature (see the top-level description).

connect.description: Write the MCP client config that wires the harness to the host wraptool (postCreate). Set false to wire it yourself (e.g. host-side `wraptool init`).

port.description: Host wraptool port, used by connect when the URL is auto-detected.

url.description: Explicit wraptool base URL for connect (e.g. http://172.18.0.1:8717). Empty = auto-detect the host as the container's default-route gateway.

//: HOME is pinned to the shared-pool mount target (/home/wraptool-harness — a dedicated user-space home, not a system /opt path). PATH gains the pool runtime's bin dir, appended (never prepended — pool tools must not shadow project tools, mirroring §12.1's rule). Both are feature invariants, not gated by a toggle: devcontainer features can't conditionalize containerEnv on an option value, and containerEnv is the layer that actually survives `devcontainer exec` (remoteEnv is reverted by its user-env probe). install.sh only creates the HOME dir (so it is valid even without a mount) and stages connect.sh; it installs no packages and makes no network access. `wraptool up` bind-mounts the host pool's home/ ($XDG_DATA_HOME/wraptool/harness-pool/home, per-developer XDG data) onto HOME and the pool's runtime/ (read-only) onto the PATH target; standalone Reopen-in-Container declares the same mounts (see examples/devcontainer, design/harness/unified-harness-pool.md §12.3).
